entries.text: In the UK, drive on the left side of the road. Steer smoothly and hold a steady line away from the kerb. Move back to the left lane after overtaking on dual carriageways.
Check your mirrors and signal before pulling away or changing speed. Only pull out when the road behind and beside you is clear. Signal early enough for other drivers to react, then cancel promptly.
You must never drive faster than the road's speed limit. Street lights with no signs usually mean 30 mph in England. Slow down below the limit near schools and parked cars.
Broken double white lines mean you must give way. Check both ways and wait until main-road cars will not slow down. Creep forward slowly if parked cars block your view.
Under H2, pedestrians crossing a side road have priority. Give way to anyone waiting to cross the road you turn into. Slow down early so you can stop smoothly before the mouth.
Always finish every turn in the left lane of the new road. Keep close to the left kerb when turning left. When turning right, go past the centre before steering left.
You must stop behind the white line on red. Amber means stop unless you are too close to stop safely. Wait for green on red and amber; never turn on red.
An ASL box at traffic lights gives cyclists space ahead of cars. You must stop at the first white line on red or amber. Leave cyclists plenty of room when pulling away on green.
Flashing orange beacons warn you of a zebra crossing ahead. You must give way once someone steps onto the stripes. You must not overtake inside the white zig-zag lines.
A yellow box junction keeps busy crossroads clear. You must not enter unless your exit road is clear. You may wait inside only when turning right and blocked by oncoming cars.

In the UK, all roundabouts circulate clockwise around the central island. You must give way to traffic approaching from your right. Enter only when there is a safe gap without forcing anyone to brake.
Read lane arrows early on the approach to a two-lane roundabout. Signal left for a left exit and right for exits past straight ahead. Signal left just after passing the exit before yours.
Hold your marked lane all the way around multi-lane roundabouts. Do not drift sideways into another driver's path when leaving. Check beside you before changing lanes on a roundabout.
Cyclists may stay in the left lane even when turning right. Give cyclists on the roundabout priority and plenty of room. Never overtake a cyclist only to cut across them at an exit.
Leave at least 1.5 metres when passing a cyclist up to 30 mph. Give even more room at speeds above 30 mph. Wait behind if oncoming traffic prevents a wide, safe pass.
Keep enough space behind the car ahead to stop safely. Drop back calmly whenever another vehicle cuts into your gap. Watch brake lights far ahead so you can slow smoothly.
Drive in the left lane on a two-lane dual carriageway. Use the right lane only to overtake slower traffic or turn right. Signal early and check your blind spot before changing lanes.
At 40 mph and above, leave at least a two-second gap. Count two seconds after the car ahead passes a roadside sign. Double the gap on wet roads to allow extra braking distance.

Build up speed on the slip road to match traffic in the left lane. Give way to traffic already on the motorway and never cross solid white lines. Signal left in good time before leaving and slow down on the exit slip road.

Always drive in the left lane unless you are overtaking slower traffic. Overtake on the right, then move back left as soon as it is safe. Do not overtake on the left unless traffic is moving in slow queues.

A red X above a lane means that lane is closed. You must not drive in it. Move safely into an open lane well before passing the red X gantry. Obey variable speed limits shown in red circles and slow down for flashing amber lights.

Never stop on a motorway lane, slip road, or hard shoulder except in an emergency. If you break down, pull into an emergency area or hard shoulder. Exit away from traffic. Never put a warning triangle on a motorway, and wait behind the safety barrier.

You must switch on sidelights and rear lights between sunset and sunrise. Use headlights at night on unlit roads and dipped headlights in built-up areas. Dip your headlights when meeting oncoming traffic or following closely so you do not dazzle.

In wet weather, stopping distances are at least double those on dry roads. Leave at least a four-second gap behind the vehicle ahead in rain and spray. Ease off the accelerator if steering feels light, and watch for pedestrians and cyclists.

You must use headlights when visibility drops below 100 metres. You may use fog lights in thick fog. Switch them off when visibility improves. Drive slowly enough to stop well within the distance you can see clearly.

The real driving test starts with an eyesight check and two safety questions. You then drive for about 35 minutes on varied roads. This includes 20 to 35 minutes of independent driving by signs or sat nav. You also complete one reversing exercise, plus an optional emergency stop. This game covers the driving and independent driving parts across Wolverhampton.

Expect a mix of residential streets, roundabouts, and faster main roads near a test centre. Watch for parked cars, narrow industrial estate exits, and sudden speed-limit changes. Official driving test routes are not published, so practise reading signs and markings early. Keep calm and follow independent driving directions safely, even if you miss a turn.
